correctness.rationale: The finite row normal form is reconstructed from the semi-Heyting identities and corroborated by separate exhaustive small-chain enumeration. Exact row multiplicities yield independent gaps. Uniform factorial-tail estimates show mean exceedance asymptotic and squared-probability sum tending to zero, giving Poisson total-variation convergence. Stirling plus union and zero-count bounds give maximum localization; first and second moment bounds give empirical and mean laws. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full-to-unary top-implication forgetful map is naturally defined on a core logical algebra. The exact law leads to a nontrivial universal factorial extreme threshold and empirical distribution and reveals strong sampling-measure bias: typical gaps remain bounded for uniform full expansions but are order n for uniform unary reducts. These provide mathematically interpretable asymptotic facts, not arbitrary table entries.
